title: Reuse vs Premature Generalization
learningObjectives: Explain when code reuse can reduce duplication.
Recognize abstractions created before a real need exists.
Compare a direct solution with a generalized one.
Use evidence of repeated behavior to guide reuse.
Avoid making speculative frameworks for one use case.

understand.concept: Reuse can reduce duplication and keep behavior consistent when multiple callers share a real need. Premature generalization happens when code is abstracted for hypothetical future cases before the current problem is understood. It often creates extra parameters, indirection, and difficult concepts. Start with the simplest clear solution, notice actual repetition or variation, and extract a reusable abstraction when it improves the design. Duplication is not always harmful if the duplicated pieces represent different concepts or are likely to change independently.
understand.whyItMatters: Design habits that support clarity, safe changes, and sustainable learning help programs remain understandable as requirements evolve.
understand.analogy: Think of maintaining a shared workspace: clear organization makes it easier to improve without disrupting others.
understand.analogyLimit: Software behavior is governed by language rules and dependencies, so the workspace analogy is only a way to reason about organization.

explain.narrative: A reusable helper is valuable when it has a clear contract and multiple meaningful callers. Don't create a configurable utility with many switches just because two snippets look similar. Consider how callers use the code, whether the shared behavior is stable, and whether the abstraction makes the next change easier. Reuse should reduce total complexity, not merely line count.

commonMistakes: Confusing a design improvement with a behavior change.
Making abstractions too broad or too narrow.
Ignoring tests and boundary behavior during changes.
Applying a guideline mechanically without considering the project's scale.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: Find two repeated snippets and one superficially similar snippet with a different purpose. Compare their behavior and likely change reasons. Extract only the stable shared behavior into a function. Keep distinct concepts separate even if their formulas match. Explain what complexity was removed and what was not generalized.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Build a small program with two genuinely repeated operations. Extract a reusable helper with a narrow contract. Add one speculative parameter, then decide whether to remove it. Show the simpler and generalized versions. Write a short rationale for the abstraction boundary.
